pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Debt has stepped up faster than earnings, and the leverage reading depends on the definition. GFL carried CAD 11,696.4 million of debt before deferred costs at September 30, 2026, up from CAD 7,426.7 million at year-end 2025 [CP-1 financial table], while trailing Adjusted EBITDA is CAD 2,257.1 million and includes SECURE for only the month after its September 1, 2026 closing [CP-1 chart data: leverage]. Unadjusted, that is 5.18x total and 5.05x net; management's run-rate basis adds CAD 730.9 million to reach 3.8x [CP-1]. The revolver test is 5.00x for four quarters after a Material Acquisition and management states compliance, but the agreement's own definitions are not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable and the unadjusted figure should not be read as a breach [CP-1 liquidity and covenants]. This is Analyst Interpretation resting on Documentary Fact figures.

Operating performance is solid but growth is bought and priced rather than volume-led. In Q3 2026 revenue rose 27.2%, of which acquisitions were 18.7% and organic 7.4%, with price 5.7% and volume (0.1)% [CP-1A company and operating model]. Adjusted EBITDA was CAD 678.7 million, up from CAD 535.1 million, at a 31.5% margin against 31.6% a year earlier, while the USA segment margin fell 2.3 points and Canada rose 2.1 points. Net loss from continuing operations was CAD 409.8 million for nine months 2026 against income of CAD 123.5 million, driven by CAD 482.9 million of interest and other finance costs and non-cash foreign exchange and fair-value charges, so earnings quality rests on the management measure [CP-1].

Cash flow covers interest on a management basis but with less room than the headline. Interest paid in cash was CAD 371.7 million for nine months 2026 against Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 1,748.4 million, a 4.70x ratio, and Q3 cash interest of CAD 172.5 million was 46.1% above CAD 118.1 million a year earlier [CP-1 chart data: interest cover; Calculations]. Adjusted EBITDA excludes CAD 172.1 million of cash costs (transaction, integration and Founder and CEO cash remuneration) for nine months 2026, and Adjusted Free Cash Flow of CAD 484.9 million is a management measure after add-backs; operating cash flow was CAD 950.1 million after a CAD 193.1 million working-capital outflow [CP-1].

Liquidity and the maturity profile are manageable near term. Cash is CAD 296.5 million and the derived revolver availability is CAD 809.7 million to CAD 1,157.0 million, depending on how letters of credit are allocated; the revolver matures on April 29, 2030 and the Term Loan B Facility on August 28, 2033 [CP-1 liquidity]. The named maturities cluster in 2028 to 2031, totalling CAD 7,621.4 million, or 65.2% of debt before deferred costs (Calculations), so refinancing capacity in those years will matter [CP-1 chart data: debt maturities].

Claims outside Note 7 debt add to the burden: lease obligations of CAD 705.0 million, closure and post-closure obligations of CAD 1,503.8 million, letters of credit of CAD 535.1 million, performance bonds of CAD 2,324.1 million, and new crude oil transportation commitments of CAD 561.4 million with onerous storage commitments of CAD 51.0 million that did not exist at year-end 2025 [CP-1 claims outside the debt figure; CP-1A company and operating model]. Pensions, factoring and litigation funding were not found in the interim sources.

Ownership and governance are unresolved rather than adverse. A Special Committee is reviewing unsolicited take-private proposals, with updated proposals due on November 9, 2026, after the cutoff, and no terms are supplied [CP-1A transaction summary]. Documented actions are mixed: nine-month 2025 share repurchases of CAD 2,758.5 million against CAD 71.0 million in 2026, and a cash payment to the Founder and CEO of CAD 74.2 million in place of share-unit settlement [CP-1A ownership, governance and behaviour]. No sponsor, ratings or control-rights information is supplied.

runs.text: Strengths. First, recurring route-based revenue: collection is 60.9% of gross revenue for nine months 2026, which gives revenue visibility even though contract terms are not supplied (Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Fact rows [CP-1A company and operating model]). Second, pricing power in the reported numbers: Q3 2026 price of 5.7% and surcharges of 1.5% drove organic growth of 7.4%, and the nine-month Adjusted EBITDA margin was 30.4% against 29.9% (Documentary Fact [CP-1A; CP-1]). Third, funding diversification and a staggered profile: a revolver to April 2030, a Term Loan B Facility to August 2033 and eight series of notes with maturities from 2028 to 2034, with no named instrument due before 2028 (Documentary Fact [CP-1 debt instruments]). Fourth, cash conversion improved on the management measure, with Adjusted Free Cash Flow of CAD 484.9 million against CAD 331.3 million (Management Language [CP-1]). Fifth, covenant compliance is stated by the issuer at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact, issuer assertion [CP-1 liquidity and covenants]). Sixth, an independent committee process governs the take-private review (Documentary Fact [CP-1A ownership, governance and behaviour]).

Weaknesses. First, leverage: debt before deferred costs rose by CAD 4,269.7 million in nine months and unadjusted leverage is 5.18x total and 5.05x net, both above the 5.00x covenant level although the covenant uses its own definitions, with the run-rate figure of 3.8x resting on CAD 730.9 million of management adjustments (Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Fact figures [CP-1]). Second, acquisition dependence and integration risk: acquisitions were 18.7% of Q3 growth, SECURE accounting is provisional, and Canada segment goodwill and indefinite-life intangibles rose from CAD 1,942.0 million to CAD 6,902.2 million (Documentary Fact [CP-1A]). Third, soft volume and a falling USA margin: volume was (0.1)% in Q3 2026 and (0.6)% for nine months 2026, and the USA margin fell 2.3 points (Documentary Fact [CP-1A]). Fourth, earnings quality: CAD 172.1 million of cash costs are added back and the nine-month net loss from continuing operations was CAD 409.8 million (Documentary Fact [CP-1]). Fifth, a rising interest burden: Q3 cash interest of CAD 172.5 million against CAD 118.1 million a year earlier, while Adjusted EBITDA rose 26.8% (Documentary Fact [CP-1]). Sixth, new energy-linked commitments: crude oil transportation commitments of CAD 561.4 million coincide with the SECURE closing but the sources do not tie them to it (Analyst Interpretation [CP-1A]). Seventh, unresolved ownership: the take-private review could change financing and covenants, and control rights are Insufficient Information (Management Language on the review; Insufficient Information on control [CP-1A]).

runs.text: The principal transaction is the acquisition of SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp. A definitive agreement was entered on April 12, 2026 (On April 12, 2026, GFL entered into a definitive agreement pursuant to which it has agreed to acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares of SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp. (Q1FS page:15)), with consideration satisfied by a combination of subordinate voting shares and cash. Management said SECURE shareholders approved it in May (SECURE shareholders approved the transaction in May (Q2PR page:1), Management Language), and it closed on September 1, 2026 for total consideration of approximately 5,414.1, of which 4,334.8 was shares and 1,079.3 cash, with 77,708,769 subordinate voting shares issued in the nine months (Q3FS page:6 and page:16). SECURE is described as an operator of waste processing, industrial waste disposal and recycling located in Western Canada and North Dakota (Q3FS page:7). The purchase price allocation is provisional: goodwill recognized for SECURE is 4,968.1, property and equipment 1,616.9, other long-term liabilities 1,006.6 and closure obligations 271.8 (Q3FS page:6), and adjustments may significantly impact the recognized values of intangible assets, goodwill, property and equipment and deferred income tax liabilities (Q3FS page:7). SECURE net working capital includes cash of 73.4. No source identifies a sponsor. A SECURE nominee joins the board, which grows to nine directors (Q3PR page:2). The status is completed, with provisional accounting.

Other acquisitions: GFL acquired 13 businesses in nine months 2026 including SECURE (the note says each is individually immaterial except SECURE), 3 in Q1 and 10 for the six months, so 3 in Q3 including SECURE. Total net assets acquired in the nine months were 7,012.6 including SECURE, of which others 1,598.5, with 2,569.8 of cash paid net of cash acquired. This corrects the CP-1 handoff, which described the 13 as other businesses besides SECURE; the note's wording and the six-month count of 10 indicate the 13 includes SECURE. Management describes year-to-date completed acquisitions as generating approximately 2 billion of annualized revenue (Q3PR page:1, Management Language). Pro forma nine-month revenue as if all 2026 acquisitions had occurred on January 1, 2026 would have been 6,905.3 against 5,746.9 reported (Q3FS page:8).

New debt in 2026, as documented in the interim debt notes (use of proceeds is not stated in any source, so purpose is Insufficient Information; the cash flow statement shows 6,795.9 issued and 3,823.9 repaid in nine months 2026): the 5.500% 2034 Notes appear first on the March 31, 2026 balance sheet at 1,393.9 (Q1FS page:8), the 5.625% 2031 Notes first on the June 30, 2026 balance sheet at 1,065.8 (Q2FS page:10) with a cross-currency swap on June 25, 2026, and the Term Loan B Facility was entered on August 28, 2026, maturing August 28, 2033 at SOFR plus 2.000%, carried at 1,418.8, with a swap fixing 5.009%. Exact issue dates, USD principal amounts and guarantors of the notes and the Term Loan B Facility are Not supplied. The revolving credit agreement was amended and restated through September 1, 2026, with a maturity of April 29, 2030 (Q3FS page:12). Liquidity effect and leverage effect are in the CP-1 handoff: total debt 11,696.4 against 7,426.7 at year-end 2025, unadjusted total debt over trailing Adjusted EBITDA of 5.18x and management Net Leverage of 3.8x.

Earlier history relevant to credit: effective March 1, 2025 GFL divested its Environmental Services line of business, retaining an option to repurchase the balance (GFL has the option to repurchase the balance of the equity of GFL Environmental Services (the “Call Option”). (Q3FS page:8)); the Call Option had a fair value of 95.0 at September 30, 2026 against 140.0 at year-end 2025. The nine-month 2025 cash flow shows divestiture proceeds of 5,817.1, long-term debt repayments of 4,294.0 and share repurchases of 2,758.5 (Q3FS page:4); the equity statement shows 40,327,898 shares repurchased and cancelled for 2,813.6 (Q3FS page:3). The relationship continues commercially: revenue from GFL Environmental Services of 29.1 for nine months 2026 and net payables of 13.7 (Q3FS page:19).

Events after the period: the Q3 statements contain no subsequent-events note. The Q3 release dated October 28, 2026 states that we formed a Special Committee of independent directors to review unsolicited inbound proposals to take the Company private (Q3PR page:1) with a final deadline of November 9, 2026 to deliver their updated proposals (Q3PR page:1). That date is after the 2026-11-05 cutoff and is a future term. The same release says there is no assurance a proposal will be received or negotiations will result in binding agreements (Q3PR page:6). The first disclosure was the July 29, 2026 release (unsolicited preliminary expressions of interest from multiple parties to take the company private (Q2PR page:2)). Bidders, price, financing and any change-of-control terms are Not supplied, so no effect on the debt documents can be assessed.

fields.value: The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for all four requested consumers. Coverage is strong for the latest quarter and the three quarters before it: five interim documents give statements, notes, segment data and non-IFRS reconciliations in CAD under IFRS, and the Q3 pair supplies the debt table, covenant wording, letters of credit, performance bonds and commodity commitments. The strongest contrary evidence is that the only annual document is a filing cover page whose exhibits are not retained, so FY2025 is available only as year-end balance sheet comparatives (which were revised after the first quarter) and as management's trailing-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA for 2025. No legal financing document is supplied, so covenant definitions, guarantor groups, security packages and call terms rest on interim-note summaries. The next evidence action is to add the FY2025 annual report exhibits (audited statements, MD&A, annual information form) and the revolving credit agreement and note indentures if available; absent that, downstream modules must carry the limitations below and label every FY2025 figure as a comparative or trailing-twelve-month figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Period coverage. Statements and notes exist for Q1 (three months), Q2 (three and six months) and Q3 (three and nine months) of 2026, each with comparative periods of 2025, so discrete quarters and quarter versus year-to-date distinctions are separable. FY2025 as a full period is covered only through management's trailing-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA (`Trailing twelve months Adjusted EBITDA(2) 2,257.1 1,985.0` (Q3PR page:14)).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Perimeter. All figures are consolidated GFL. Equity-method associates, including the retained stake in the divested environmental services business (`GFL has the option to repurchase the balance of the equity of GFL Environmental Services (the “Call Option”).` (Q3FS page:8)), sit outside Adjusted EBITDA by definition of the add-back. Non-wholly-owned subsidiaries carry stand-alone credit facilities inside long-term debt (`Certain of GFL’s non-wholly owned subsidiaries have stand alone credit facilities included in other in long-term debt.` (Q3FS page:13)). The issuer-versus-restricted-group distinction is not drawn in any source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt. The Q3 debt note lists the revolving credit facility, the Term Loan B Facility, eight series of USD notes (two of them secured at issue, one since released from collateral), the tax-exempt bonds and other facilities, and totals `Total long-term debt 11,671.4 7,422.6` (Q3FS page:11) in CAD millions for September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025. Maturities appear in the footnotes, not in a year-by-year table.

fields.value: - Covenants. `equal to or less than 5.00 to 1.00 for a period of four complete fiscal quarters following completion of a Material Acquisition` (Q3FS page:13) applies to Total Net Funded Debt to Adjusted EBITDA, with `GFL was in compliance with these covenants.` (Q3FS page:13). The ratio as defined in the agreement is not printed.

Pension and retiree medical obligations: no mention found in any source (searched "pension", "retirement", "post-employment").

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management claims. Guidance, run-rate EBITDA, Net Leverage and Adjusted Free Cash Flow are management non-IFRS measures; guidance has no reconciliation (`GFL does not have information available to provide a quantitative reconciliation of such projections` (Q3PR page:3)). They are attributed claims, not controlling facts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Q3 release states a take-private review: `Special Committee of independent directors to review unsolicited inbound proposals to take the Company private` (Q3PR page:1) with `final deadline of November 9, 2026` (Q3PR page:1). The date falls after the cutoff 2026-11-05 and is a future term, not an outcome. No proposal terms, bidders or financing are in the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Q3 statements carry no subsequent-events note (searched all seven sources for "subsequent"; only the Q1 statements have one, `Subsequent to March 31, 2026, GFL completed 5 acquisitions` (Q1FS page:15)). Events between September 30, 2026 and the cutoff are therefore evidenced only by the Q3 release dated October 28, 2026.

Downstream goodwill, intangible and net debt analysis is therefore provisional.

fields.value: GFL's financial base at September 30, 2026 is a larger, more levered consolidated group than at year-end 2025, and the leverage figure depends entirely on which EBITDA and debt definition is used. Reported debt before deferred costs rose by 4,269.7 to 11,696.4 while cash rose by 210.9 to 296.5; the increase coincides with 2,569.8 of nine-month acquisition spend, the SECURE share-and-cash purchase that closed September 1, 2026, and a Term Loan B Facility entered on August 28, 2026; the sources do not bridge the debt movement line by line. Trailing-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2,257.1 captures SECURE for one month only, so total debt over that EBITDA is 5.18x and net 5.05x, whereas management's Net Leverage of 3.8x adds 730.9 of run-rate adjustments to reach 2,988.0. The revolver covenant is 5.00x for four quarters after a Material Acquisition and 4.50x otherwise, and management states compliance; the agreement definition is not in the pack, so headroom is not calculable here and the unadjusted 5.18x must not be read as a breach. Cash conversion improved at the management-defined Adjusted Free Cash Flow level (484.9 for nine months 2026 against 331.3), but operating cash flow is stated after 193.1 of working-capital outflow and the earnings measure adds back 172.1 of cash costs. All FY2025 figures other than the year-end balance sheet comparatives and management's trailing-twelve-month figures are unavailable, and the year-end 2025 balance sheet was revised after Q1.

fields.value: - Covenants. `The Revolving Credit Agreement contains a Total Net Funded Debt to Adjusted EBITDA and an Interest Coverage Ratio (each as defined in the Revolving Credit Agreement) financial maintenance covenant.` (Q3FS page:12). The metric computed here differs from the covenant: it uses unadjusted trailing Adjusted EBITDA, debt before deferred costs and cash netting, while the agreement defines Total Net Funded Debt and Adjusted EBITDA itself, and the release says Run-Rate EBITDA is `calculated in accordance with the terms of our revolving credit agreement` (Q3PR page:10).

Second, acquisition dependence and integration risk: acquisitions were 18.7% of Q3 growth, SECURE accounting is provisional, and Canada segment goodwill and indefinite-life intangibles rose from CAD 1,942.0 million to CAD 6,902.2 million (Documentary Fact [CP-1A]). Third, soft volume and a falling USA margin: volume was (0.1)% in Q3 2026 and (0.6)% for nine months 2026, and the USA margin fell 2.3 points (Documentary Fact [CP-1A]). Fourth, earnings quality: CAD 172.1 million of cash costs are added back and the nine-month net loss from continuing operations was CAD 409.8 million (Documentary Fact [CP-1]). Fifth, a rising interest burden: Q3 cash interest of CAD 172.5 million against CAD 118.1 million a year earlier, while Adjusted EBITDA rose 26.8% (Documentary Fact [CP-1]). Sixth, new energy-linked commitments: crude oil transportation commitments of CAD 561.4 million coincide with the SECURE closing but the sources do not tie them to it (Analyst Interpretation [CP-1A]). Seventh, unresolved ownership: the take-private review could change financing and covenants, and control rights are Insufficient Information (Management Language on the review; Insufficient Information on control [CP-1A]).
